Eve: Quick follow-up to the probabilistic selector RFC — thinking about how we cap degeneracy when cache/kv hits push one variant to >90% traffic.
Kai: Agree, saw that in the sim. We get mode collapse where "fast" wins and cheap/regional starve.
Maya: Short idea: add a soft entropy floor that forces exploration every N requests. cheap can get occasional samples.
Eve: Exactly. Also want to consider tenant-level guarantees: a tenant with SLA=low shouldn't suddenly see all fast expensive models.
Zane: We already have tenant-priority weight; but that's multiplicative. When a model has much lower latency it dominates.
Priya: Can we do a "degeneration rate" metric exposed in telemetry? e.g. fraction of requests where top-1 weight > 0.9 over 5m.
infra-bot: Deploy queued: canary/prob-selector v0.2 -> testbed (sha: abcd1234)
Kai: here's a rough config sketch:
```
selector:
  type: probabilistic
  entropy_floor: 0.05 # min entropy to keep exploration
  decay_window_ms: 300000
  tenant_safety:
    max_shift: 0.2
    enforcement: soft
```
Maya: enforcement: soft = emit warning + soft-penalty; hard = reject policy change, right?
Kai: yes. Soft will nudge weights by KL-penalty during normalization.
Eve: Also need an emergency degrader path: if top model fails, fallback to cheapest compatible. But that shouldn't be used to game the selector.
Zane: thought: instead of absolute entropy floor, use per-tenant adaptive floor proportional to request volume.
Priya: we should also add a small deterministic seed for A/B: e.g., sample hash(user_id) % 100 to keep stable assignments for sessions.
Eve: Good call. Can we list follow-ups: 1) define "degeneration_rate" metric & alerting 2) implement entropy_floor + per-tenant scaling 3) telemetry-backed canary runs 4) update rollout policy to include soft-penalty knob
Kai: I'll open PR with unit tests and sim harness for collapse cases.
Maya: I can add telemetry queries and dashboards.
Eve: Thanks — will sync in architecture sync Thursday. :thumbsup:
